title: Shared Cryptographic Credentials Across Geodistributed Nodes
pattern: Deploying a single, shared cryptographic private key or TLS certificate globally across all application servers and geographic database centers.
why_bad: Fails the compartment isolation principle. If an attacker physically or logically compromises a single host in a remote branch, they gain the keys necessary to decrypt traffic, forge signatures, or impersonate nodes across the entire global infrastructure.
detection: The deployment of identical binary images containing hardcoded keys, or shared file paths syncing identical master certificates to all regional clusters.
fix: Compartmentalize key distribution: provision isolated, host-specific or location-specific credentials to individual servers, enabling agile revocation of compromised nodes without affecting the rest of the fleet.
source: `Heather Adkins et al. - Building Secure and Reliable Systems (2020)`, Ch 8, p. 158.
